etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French intrinsèque, from Latin intrīnsecus (“on the inside, inwardly”), from *intrim, an assumed adverbial form of inter (“within”) + secus (“by, on the side”).
senses: Innate, inherent, inseparable from the thing itself, essential.
(physics, of a variable) With a quantity that does not depend on the amount of matter present
(computing, programming) A built-in function that is implemented directly by the compiler, without any intermediate call to a library.
(video games) An ability possessed by a character and not requiring any external equipment.
